extracted.intended_audience: USPTO-registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys and agents); counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedures, and criteria used by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline to evaluate alleged practitioner misconduct (financial/accounting violations) and to approve settlement agreements and impose sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is subject to USPTO Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) are subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states Respondent (a registered patent practitioner) is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and 37 C.F.R. §10.20 et seq., establishing that these rules govern practitioner conduct before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement approval and scope (37 C.F.R. § 11.26; 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement submitted to the USPTO Director must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and the Director has authority under 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26 to approve such agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement should set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and may resolve all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts. The Office may approve and issue a Final Order reflecting the agreed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on depositing unearned fees into business/operating account (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not deposit client funds that are unearned fees for legal services into the practitioner's business/operating account; such funds should be segregated (e.g., in a trust account).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically cites violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a) for depositing, at times, unearned fees into a business/operating account. It notes one permitted exception: 'other than advances for costs and expenses' (i.e., advances for costs/expenses may be handled differently).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to maintain complete and sufficiently formal accounting records (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep complete, sufficiently formal accounting records for deposits into and disbursements from their accounts (including client funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent was found to have not maintained sufficiently formal accounting records. Remedial/accounting practices (ledger with separate pages per client, electronic accounting system) are described as corrective measures. Financial institutions' reporting of NSF items can trigger audits by the bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting checks returned for insufficient funds (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not submit checks to the USPTO (or otherwise) that are drawn on accounts with insufficient funds; submitting such checks violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes eight checks drawn on Respondent's business/operating account were returned for insufficient funds (totaling $3,569). The fact that Respondent later made good on the checks and no client harm appears is treated as relevant mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and specific discipline imposed (public reprimand; publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose public discipline such as a public reprimand and order publication of the reprimand in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the agreed discipline was a public reprimand; the OED Director was ordered to publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and to publish a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette. The Final Order spells out the wording of the Notice of Reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of discipline to courts and disciplinary agencies (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director must notify disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the practitioner is admitted, courts where admitted, and the public of the public-discipline and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts where Respondent is admitted and identifies § 11.59 as the governing regulation for such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered as mitigating in sanction determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating factors include length of registered practice, absence of prior disciplinary history, acceptance of responsibility and remorse, remedial steps taken, lack of client harm, and restitution where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists specific mitigating factors: Respondent had been a registered practitioner for over 25 years with no prior disciplinary history; he accepted responsibility and was remorseful; he made good on returned checks and clients appear not harmed; and he adopted improvements to fund handling that exceed USPTO requirements (e.g., placing advances for costs/expenses in trust account). These factors were reflected in the agreed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial measures that mitigate discipline (recommended/cited corrective actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial actions that can mitigate discipline include consulting with counsel about ethics rules, establishing/maintaining a client trust account, obtaining a bank agreement to report NSF trust-account items, keeping a ledger with separate pages per client, maintaining an electronic accounting system for client funds, employing a bookkeeper, and retaining a law practice management consultant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's remedial actions are detailed: consulted another attorney and became thoroughly versed in rules on financial recordkeeping and segregation of client funds; bank agreed to report returned trust-account checks to NY State Lawyer's Fund for Client Protection (triggering bar audits); established client-specific ledgers and electronic accounting; employed a part-time bookkeeper; retained a law-practice management consultant. These actions were accepted as mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client harm and restitution as factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the conduct resulted in harm to clients and whether the practitioner made restitution (made good on returned checks and fees) are relevant to discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes it does not appear the NSF checks resulted in harm to clients and that Respondent made good on all returned checks and fees; these facts were considered mitigating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and access to disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL given) and may be made publicly accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order commands publication of the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and describes that disciplinary decisions are posted there. The Notice of Reprimand language is provided as an example of what will be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties to a settlement agreement may agree on allocation of costs, including that each party bears its own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this settlement the OED Director and Respondent agreed to bear their own costs; the Final Order memorializes that agreement.
